<a id="body"></a>

## Body

Normal native-session supersession can leave a retired predecessor and live successor sharing the same PID, process start and pane. Those process checks, even with a pane root older than the process, do not establish exclusive seat ownership. Another live registry holder must veto a kill-pane hint before the process-based Own classification. The close prints advice; it does not kill the process itself.

PR #220 closed S220-001 at 59a35cdc15271eeffc5dab63c5178c53ec108ebd; output 866fa8fd9383ae030132b5868e3e112e43b98fd7. The test uses identical predecessor/successor bindings. Unreadable pane details produce no kill hint; control-client parse failures check the live pane list without launching a client. Holder names use render::seat.

S220-N003 remains a C34 follow-up: registry-list .ok() still treats a read error as no other holder. Do not claim every observation failure is fail-closed.

The designated-prime dead-orphan exception comes from projects.prime_id only, requires a parentless seat and observed dead/recycled process, and must be shared with the held memory-turn continuation. The store compares the exact observed descriptor before closing. Old blanket "close then kill-pane" advice needs these qualifications.
